title: Runtime Execution Orchestra: Scheduler Synthesis, Profiling Playbook, and Benchmarking Matrix
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview

This playbook synthesizes cross-cutting runtime concerns into a single, experiment-driven operational guide: how the Scheduler (scheduler-service) integrates with the Execution Orchestra (runtime-orchestrator), how we profile scheduler and kernel behaviour end-to-end, and a compact benchmarking matrix to validate tuning changes before rollout. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and profiling squad members.

Goals

- Provide deterministic, repeatable steps to evaluate scheduler changes and their impact on tail latency, cost, and kernel utilization.
- Standardize profiling hygiene for scheduling experiments so results are comparable across clusters.
- Define a lightweight benchmark matrix that exercises common production shapes and quantization variants.

Service & Component Inventory

- runtime-orchestrator: control plane that composes kernel dispatch plans and routes requests to kernel-dispatcher.
- scheduler-service: admission controller and slot allocator; implements priority buckets and credit accounting.
- kernel-dispatcher: GPU-side dispatcher that executes mapped kernels.
- kvcache-service: shared KV cache with warmup and eviction telemetry hooks.
- request-classifier: sidecar component that assigns incoming requests to pre-configured execution cohorts.

Key Performance Targets (SLOs)

- Stability SLO (short requests, seq <= 64): p99 latency <= 250ms; p95 <= 80ms.
- Long-sequence SLO (seq 512): p99 <= 2.2s; p95 <= 1.1s.
- Kernel tail safety: no single kernel should have >15% invocation rate variance across active slots for a sustained 10-minute window.
- Cost SLO: per-token GPU time change <= +10% after scheduler changes for steady-state mixed workloads.

Experiment Matrix and Benchmarking Table

Run each experiment in a dedicated canary cluster or shadow lane. The matrix below covers three canonical workload shapes: interactive chat (short), document summarization (long), and embeddings mix (small dense batches).

| Workload               | Seq len | Concurrency | Kernel hint    | Quant profile | Key metrics collected               |
|------------------------|---------|-------------|----------------|---------------|-------------------------------------|
| Interactive Chat       | 8-64    | 50-300      | small-attn     | q4f           | p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec     |
| Document Summarization | 256-1024| 10-40       | sharded-attn   | fp16 / q8_1   | p95/p99 latency, kernel-util, evicts|
| Embeddings Mix         | 1-32    | 100-1000    | dense-matmul   | fp16          | throughput, kernel-queue-length     |

Benchmarking notes:
- Use the operational-workload-simulator with the same request provenance headers used in prod to ensure equivalence.
- For each cell run: 10m warmup, 30m steady-state sampling, 5m cool-down.

Profiling Playbook (step-by-step)

1) Prepare the environment
   - Reserve a canary GPU pool (tag: canary-scheduler-experiment).
   - Deploy the candidate scheduler binary behind a feature flag (flags: scheduler.new_priority_map=true).
   - Ensure kvcache-service telemetry is at debug level for the experiment window.

2) Baseline capture (control)
   - Run the benchmark matrix against current production scheduler.
   - Collect kernel traces (ktrace), scheduler traces, and kvcache hit-rate histograms.
   - Commands (example):

   # Start a profiler capture (example CLI)
   infra-cli profiler start --service scheduler-service --session experiment-run-001 --duration 40m

   # Start kernel dispatcher trace (on canary nodes)
   node-ctl trace start --target kernel-dispatcher --label canary-scheduler-experiment --out /tmp/ktrace-control.pb

3) Candidate capture (treatment)
   - Flip the feature flag and re-run the same benchmark cells. Keep all other infra constants identical.
   - Capture the same traces and aggregate.

4) Signal extraction
   - Extract the following per-request signals: scheduler_decision_time_ms, kernel_enqueue_delay_ms, kvcache_lookup_time_ms, and overall_end_to_end_latency_ms.
   - Use the trace-correlation utility:

   trace-corr --input /tmp/ktrace-control.pb,/tmp/ktrace-treatment.pb --keys request_id --out /tmp/trace-diff.json

5) Attribution checks
   - For any latency regression >10% at p95 or p99: construct causal hypothesis and search for correlated spikes in kernel_enqueue_delay_ms or priority-rebalancing events.
   - Check kernel utilization per-GPU and per-kernel type. If a single kernel shows >25% uplift in p99 execution time, tag as kernel-regression.

6) Quality gates
   - Block rollout if: p99 regression > 15% on short workloads OR kernel tail safety SLO violated.
   - Soft rollout allowed if cost delta <= +5% and p99 regression < 10%, with live monitoring for 24h.

Observability & Telemetry Contract

Every scheduler experiment must emit the following metrics at 10s and 1m resolution:
- scheduler.admit_latency_ms.p95, p99
- scheduler.slot_fill_ratio (0-1)
- scheduler.priority_rebalances.count
- kernel.dispatch_queue_length.avg
- kvcache.evictions_per_minute
- request.cohort_end_to_end_latency.p50,p95,p99

Trace annotations (required):
- scheduler_decision_id: unique id for scheduler decision that can be correlated to kernel events.
- kernel_dispatch_id: id assigned by kernel-dispatcher.
- cohort_label: the request-classifier cohort name.

Runbook: Incident Triage (scheduling-related)

Symptoms: sudden p99 rise in short requests, excess scheduler.rebalance events, disproportionate kernel queue length on a subset of nodes.

Immediate actions (0-10m)
1. Page runtime-oncall and @runtime-platform Slack channel.
2. Activate runbook channel (ops-channel: #runtime-incidents).
3. Toggle scheduler -> safe-mode: infra-cli flag set-scheduler-mode safe (falls back to admission-by-cost).
4. Re-route new traffic to backup GPU pool (tag: fallback-dedicated) using runtime-orchestrator policy: runtime-orchestrator route --policy fallback-dedicated --reason "incident".

Diagnostic steps (10-45m)
- Capture a 15m trace of scheduler decisions and kernel dispatch traces.
- Run quick histogram diff: trace-diff-analyzer --metric scheduler.admit_latency_ms --window 15m
- Check for: priority inversion signals, KV cache coldness, node-level GPU thermal throttling (node-ctl metrics).

Mitigations (45m-3h)
- If priority inversion: temporarily disable low-priority bursting (scheduler-service config: allow_burst_low_starve=false).
- If kvcache cold: trigger targeted prefetch for top-10 keys per cohort (kvcache-service API: prefetch --cohort <name> --keys-file /tmp/top10.json).
- If node thermal: cordon affected nodes and shift batches using runtime-orchestrator node-drain policy.

Post-incident (3h-72h)
- Run the full profiling playbook and compare control vs incident traces.
- Create an incident postmortem with the following sections: timeline, impact, root cause hypothesis, remediation plan, roll-forward/rollback plan, owners.
- If change was due to scheduler code, revert to previous release and open a regression ticket with kernel team.

Rollout & Release Guidance

- Canary phases: alpha (1 node), small-canary (5 nodes), canary-pool (20 nodes), fleet-rollout (gradual 5% increments every 6h).
- Required sign-offs: runtime-platform lead, kernel-owner, SRE on-call.
- Monitoring checklist before each percentage bump: p95 and p99 within thresholds, no new error signatures in scheduler logs, eviction rate stable.

Configuration Examples

1) scheduler-service config (YAML snippet)

scheduler:
  mode: "priority"               # priority | cost | safe
  slot_size_ms: "8"            # nominal slot unit
  max_slots_per_gpu: "64"
  allow_burst_low_starve: "true"
  rebalance_window_s: "30"
  credit_decay_s: "300"

2) runtime-orchestrator route policy (JSON example)

{ "policy_name": "fallback-dedicated", "criteria": ["latency>200ms","load>0.85"], "actions": ["reroute_pool:dedicated-03","notify:sre-team"] }

Known Issues & Short-term Workarounds

- Issue: transient priority oscillation when slot_size_ms is less than kernel microbatch latency.
  Workaround: increase slot_size_ms to 12ms for affected kernel families and enable slot coalescing.

- Issue: kvcache prefetch storms during synchronized warmups cause eviction spikes.
  Workaround: stagger cohort warmup by 10-30s using request-classifier delay window.

- Issue: scheduler metrics undercount when trace sampling is set below 2%.
  Workaround: temporarily raise sampling to 10% during experiments.

Appendix: Experiment templates and expected artifacts

- Required artifacts for every scheduler experiment: control and treatment ktrace pb, aggregated trace-diff.json, metric rollup CSV (10s/1m), experiment runbook with hypothesis, and JIRA ticket linking artifacts.

- Template command to upload artifacts to experiment bucket:

  infra-cli artifact upload --session experiment-run-001 --files /tmp/ktrace-control.pb,/tmp/trace-diff.json --bucket gs://runtime-experiments/2025-03-12/experiment-run-001

- Minimum artifact retention: 90 days for cross-reference during regressions.
